messages.author: 22adcb01926131d1
messages.subject: blavaan output error
parts:
Hello!

I'm trying to run some models I've ran previously without error but recently I've been getting a persistent error.

test.mod <- '
DV1 ~ IV
DV2 ~ IV
DV3 ~ IV
DV4 ~ IV'

### Fitting models
simpleuninf.fit <- bsem(model =  test.mod, data = clean) # uninformative
simplelowinf.fit <- bsem(model = test.mod, data = clean, dp = dpriors(beta = "normal(0.5,0.447)")) # informative
simplehighinf.fit <- bsem(model = test.mod, data = clean, dp = dpriors(beta = "normal(0.5, 0.316)")) # informative

In each of those cases, I get the following error when I try to view the summary:

Error in parsumm$summary[newpt$stansumnum[pte2], "97.5%"] : 
  subscript out of bounds

Also, on occasion, the output in the console when running any model is limited to the following:
blavaan (0.3-12) results of 1000 samples after 500 adapt/burnin iterations

                                                  Used       Total
  Number of observations                           526         800

  Number of missing patterns                         1

  Statistic                                 MargLogLik         PPP
  Value                                      -3102.893       0.492

Additional info: all the DVs are continuous, and the IV is a binary coded categorical variable. 

What am I missing?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: blavaan output error
parts:
About the console output: I have heard this sometimes happening to other people, but have not been able to sysematically reproduce it. It seems to happen to people who run multiple models in one Rstudio session. Aside from restarting Rstudio (or R, if you are not using Rstudio), I'm not sure what to recommend.

About the error from your model: are you able to share the data or show the output of str(clean)? I suspect the problem is related to the categorical IV.

Ed

parts:
For everyone's reference: the error seems to disappear when I separate the blavaan models in a separate script in a separate session. After some trial and error, it turns out the error occurs when I set the options for the R session to 2 digits using options(digits = 2). Once I remove this setting, the output works just fine!

Hope this helps.

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: blavaan output error
parts:
On Sat, 2020-12-12 at 07:27 -0800, 'alaa....@aucegypt.edu' via blavaan wrote:
it turns out the error occurs when I set the options for the R session to 2 digits using options(digits = 2). Once I remove this setting, the output works just fine!

Just a follow-up here, it happens because the R quantile() command does funny things with naming, which led to the blavaan error. For example

> options(digits=2)
> set.seed(1)
> quantile(rnorm(50), probs=.975)
98% 
1.5 

So the name is "98%", even though it is giving you the 97.5th percentile. I think this is a good reason to avoid setting the digits option, instead trying to round in other ways. For example, in the blavaan summary() command, there is an "nd" argument that lets you specify the number of digits to display (summary(fit, nd=2)).

Ed
